key_insight: A quantum-assisted agentic DAI controller can meet hard microgrid control deadlines while solving per-slot dispatch optimally and improving cost through smarter storage valuation.
engineering_relevance: This framework is relevant for real-time renewable microgrid operation because it combines deadline-aware optimization, solver orchestration, and intertemporal storage pricing in a single control loop.
method: BDIx agents formulate each dispatch slot as a QUBO problem.
A coordinator agent selects among quantum, quantum-inspired, and classical solvers based on learned latency beliefs and deadline constraints.
A storage agent uses discounted future-peak valuation to encode intertemporal battery value.
evidence_signal: In a 24-hour simulated grid-connected microgrid, the system missed zero deadlines, achieved the exact optimum in every slot, and reached a daily cost of 146.24 EUR with 97.83% renewable utilization and zero unserved energy.
watch_item: Results rely on statevector QAOA simulation and a specific benchmark microgrid, so real hardware performance and scalability under larger, noisier deployments remain to be validated.
paper_title: A Quantum-Assisted Agentic Distributed Artificial Intelligence Framework for Deadline-Bounded Orchestration of Hybrid Renewable Microgrids
